article_notes: 32 PCR-confirmed Babesia dogs (8 B. vogeli, 12 B. gibsoni, 12 mixed) at Madras Veterinary College Teaching Hospital, plus 32 healthy controls. Outcome followed during treatment; 14 died, 18 survived; euthanasia not mentioned. Samples on day of admission before treatment. One-way ANOVA with Tukey across control/survivors/non-survivors; per-group means (SEM) only in Figs 1-5, so no per-group values extracted. Table 2 compares markers between Babesia species groups (not severity) and Table 3 gives hepcidin correlations within non-survivors (marker-marker); neither extracted. Severity groups are confounded with species (mixed infection 11/14 non-survivors).

associations.marker_as_reported: Babesia species (B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, mixed)
associations.timepoint: first day of admission, before treatment
associations.species: B. vogeli, B. gibsoni or both
associations.statistic: non-survivors: 3 B. gibsoni, 11 mixed; survivors: 8 B. vogeli, 9 B. gibsoni, 1 mixed; mortality 0% B. vogeli, 25% B. gibsoni, 91.6% mixed
associations.quote: Among the 14 non-survivors, 3 dogs had B. gibsoni infection and 11 dogs had mixed infection of B. gibsoni and B. vogeli . Out of 18 survivors, 8 dogs had B. vogeli infection, 9 dogs had B. gibsoni infection and 1 dog had a mixed infection of both. No mortality was seen in dogs with B. vogeli infection while B. gibsoni infection resulted in 25% mortality. However, in animals with mixed infection of both B. gibsoni and B. vogeli 91.6% mortality was observed
associations.note: No statistical test. Mortality highest with mixed infection, none with B. vogeli alone.
